summary: OpenAI publishes the GPT-4o system card describing a new omni-modal model accepting text, audio, image and video input and generating text, audio and image output, with stated speed, cost and safety evaluation details.

mechanisms.reason: The model is stated to be faster and 50% cheaper per API call while matching prior-generation performance, implying reduced serving cost per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: It matches GPT-4 Turbo performance on text in English and code, with significant improvement on text in non-English languages, while also being much faster and 50\% cheaper in the API.

mechanisms.reason: A single end-to-end network handling text, audio, image and video with near-human audio response latency represents a new capability class rather than an incremental refresh.
mechanisms.quote: GPT-4o can respond to audio inputs in as little as 232 milliseconds, with an average of 320 milliseconds, which is similar to human response time in conversation.

practices.reason: Engineering teams building on GPT-4o gain a cheaper, faster, natively multimodal endpoint with real-time audio response, changing what interactive and vision/audio products are buildable.
practices.quote: GPT-4o is especially better at vision and audio understanding compared to existing models.

practices.reason: The system card documents Preparedness Framework evaluations and third-party dangerous-capability assessments that describe the lab's own safety evaluation process rather than a transferable instrument.
practices.quote: we are sharing the GPT-4o System Card, which includes our Preparedness Framework evaluations.

notable_reason: This is the primary technical documentation of GPT-4o's real-time multimodal capabilities, cost, and safety evaluations, a significant frontier release from OpenAI.
